subject: Energy
title: The Sun as Energy Source
description: A 60-second lesson on The Sun as Energy Source.

hook.text: Nearly all energy on Earth traces back to the Sun—a fusion reactor 150 million km away.

buildup.text: The Sun emits 3.8 × 10²⁶ watts—Earth intercepts about one billionth of that, yet it powers almost everything.

discovery.text: Solar energy drives the water cycle, wind, photosynthesis, and fossil fuel formation—all are stored sunlight.

twist.text: Geothermal and nuclear energy are exceptions—they come from Earth's internal heat and uranium formed in ancient stars.

climax.text: In one hour, the Sun delivers more energy to Earth's surface than humanity uses in an entire year.

punchline.text: One hour of sunlight could power civilization for a year.

quiz.question: How much solar energy hits Earth compared to human use?
options: One hour of sun equals a year of human use
The Sun provides less than we use
